content_html:
Insects enter homes looking for food, water, shelter, favorable temperature, or simply following light and airflow. Common entry routes include gaps at doors and windows, utility penetrations, damaged screens, and objects brought indoors. The species and room where it appears help identify the attraction.

Connect the insect with the room where it appears

Gnats near plants do not have the same cause as ants beside food or silverfish in a damp bathroom. Identifying the general pest group prevents using the same solution for every insect.

Food and water create an indoor reward

Crumbs, pet food, trash, drips, and condensation can sustain activity even after gaps are sealed. Clean spills, store food in closed containers, and repair water sources.

Small gaps are enough for many insects

Inspect weatherstripping, screens, cable penetrations, and siding joints. The goal is not to make the house airtight; prioritize gaps connected to areas where activity is actually seen.

Some pests arrive in boxes, plants, or food

Inspect stored cardboard, bulk foods, and new plants if the problem began after bringing items indoors. Isolating the source can solve the issue without treating the entire home.
